reviewer: Claude (independent application source review; did not author the application)
verdict: SOURCE APPROVED AGAINST THE AGREED CONTRACT, WITH NON-BLOCKING NOTES. No blocking defect found in DS1-DS5, fd3 adoption, the status protocol, stop/EOF semantics, record files or cleanup ordering. This is source evidence only. It is not runtime, Darwin descriptor, input or two-window evidence, and it is not artifact admission. The original observer and every earlier receipt and failure are unchanged.

contract_checks.fd3_adoption: PASS. main.rs:829-834: signal setup, then fcntl(3,F_GETFD), then adoption before any open can reuse fd 3. status.rs:29-72 requires: a valid lowercase hex48 instance; peer_addr succeeding (rejects non-AF_UNIX and unconnected or listening sockets); SO_TYPE==SOCK_STREAM with a checked option length (rejects datagram and seqpacket); then sets O_NONBLOCK and FD_CLOEXEC. SIGPIPE is ignored (main.rs:56), so a closed peer gives EPIPE as an error instead of killing the app. That fd 3 is the session's socket at all relies on the session's adddup2 under POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT (contract).
contract_checks.status_frames: PASS. The exact formats are status.rs:88-106. Worst-case lengths are about 78 bytes (READY) and about 98 bytes (CLEANUP), under 256. There is one FIFO with a 512-byte pending bound, so a READY queued before CLEANUP stays ahead of it. READY is refused if duplicate or after CLEANUP. CLEANUP is refused if duplicate, or if COMPLETE=1 comes with no status or a negative one. A missing status is sent as -1. COMPLETE, TERM_SENT and KILL_SENT are u8::from(bool).
contract_checks.status_nonblocking_and_bounded: PASS. pump (status.rs:108-132) is nonblocking and handles EINTR and EAGAIN, and errors 1 s after the first unsent byte. finish (133-156) is at most 250 ms with 10 ms polls. In the loop, a failure of pump (main.rs:627) or of READY (728) ends the session as stop_cause 'fault'. run() then still performs owned cleanup and final records and attempts CLEANUP. A CLEANUP or finish failure is recorded in errors, status-error.json, stderr and exit 1 (main.rs:893-904). Nothing waits on the channel unboundedly, and a channel failure never skips cleanup. Unit tests cover wrong type, broken peer, full SO_SNDBUF and the deadline (status.rs:215-248).
contract_checks.cleanup_before_cleanup_frame: PASS. run() order: pty.cleanup (main.rs:872-874), then rx/tx sync_all, whose failure forces complete=false (882-887), then result.json create-new plus fsync, whose failure forces complete=false (889-892), and only then status.cleanup and finish (893). CLEANUP is emitted only after actual PTY cleanup and synced final records. COMPLETE=1 requires a reaped raw status and no error (pty.rs:460-522).
contract_checks.readiness_without_focus: PASS. The READY gate is main.rs:721-729: exec checked, keymap parsed, SSD configure/ack, and at least one frame callback. There is no focus, held-key or modifier term. The deadline text no longer names focus (649-651). Host test Unfocused gets READY with no wl_keyboard.enter (host_wayland_tests.rs:416-420). Readiness still has a 20 s session deadline, which is a fault.
contract_checks.DS1_accepted_input_after_leave: PASS. leave() clears focus and held keys but keeps pending (input.rs:40-44). The loop keeps calling write_pending whenever pty.ready() (main.rs:730-732). Only actual successful writes are counted and transcribed. At stop, audit records input_accepted_bytes, pty_tx_bytes, input_unsent_bytes and stop_cause (784). Host test TypeLeave: the server closes only after pty-tx.bin reaches 3 bytes; the transcript is 'abc' with unsent 0 (427-431). There is also a unit test for partial write then Alt+Tab (input.rs:143).
contract_checks.DS2_DS3_focus_bookkeeping: PASS. enter() validates the held array and records it without translation. A release removes the key from held and yields no bytes (keys.rs:46-47). A held modifier across a focus change is covered (input.rs:175). Duplicate press and out-of-range keys are errors. The input quota is MAX_TX 16384 accepted bytes.
contract_checks.DS4_child_descriptors: PASS AT SOURCE LEVEL. In the child (pty.rs:155-224), stdio is dup2'd from the slave with FD_CLOEXEC cleared, and every fd from 3 to sysconf(_SC_OPEN_MAX) except the exec-status pipe is closed. The pipe was promoted to fd 3 or higher with CLOEXEC (promote, pty.rs:106-119), so it closes on successful exec. The PTY and logs are created before the Wayland connect (main.rs:847-857), and the app has no fork or exec afterwards. Darwin's non-atomic socket CLOEXEC and its SCM_RIGHTS keymap fds (no MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC) therefore cannot reach /bin/sh. The bound is sound because the app never raises RLIMIT_NOFILE and CLOEXEC_DEFAULT leaves only fds 0-3; an unlimited or out-of-range sysconf fails closed (pty.rs:280-283). The child is async-signal-safe: no allocation, mask cleared, nine signals reset to SIG_DFL including the inherited SIGPIPE ignore. The host test checks fd3, a non-CLOEXEC log, a status fd and a socket sentinel, and exec_checked still passes (pty.rs:628-646). That test reads /proc, so it is Linux-only; Darwin descriptor evidence is still required.
contract_checks.DS5_launch_chord: PASS. Held keys at enter are stored, never translated, and their releases produce nothing. Covered by unit test input.rs:127 and host test HeldLaunch (enter with held Return+Super, released after READY, empty transcript; host_wayland_tests.rs:422-425).
contract_checks.EOF_and_stop_causes: PASS. pty.read sets eof when read returns 0; the EIO-as-EOF mapping applies only off Apple (pty.rs:416-431). The pinned XNU source confirms Darwin EOF is read()==0. The last replica close reaches ttyclose, which sets t_state=0 (tty.c:448). ptcread then returns 0 when TS_CONNECTED is clear (tty_dev.c:684-685), and ptcselect reports ready (tty_dev.c:820-822). The loop reads every turn and breaks on eof (main.rs:653-679). Precedence is fault > window_close > shell_eof > signal > deadline (773-783). The normal causes return Ok without requiring READY or shell exit 0. The real wait status is kept. Host tests cover close before READY and shell EOF before READY (433-444).
contract_checks.records: PASS. private_dir (main.rs:563-575) uses symlink_metadata and requires a directory, owner euid and exact mode 0700. log() uses create_new, O_NOFOLLOW, O_CLOEXEC and mode 0600 with an explicit chmod (552-561). Tests cover two distinct directories, collision, refusal at 0755 and symlink refusal (main.rs:945-973).
contract_checks.cleanup: PASS. TERM goes to the owned group when getsid and getpgid equal the pid, otherwise to the pid; this is rechecked before KILL. Then a 250 ms grace, KILL, and a 2 s WNOHANG reap. Master and status fds are closed. The result is cached, so cleanup is idempotent. complete requires a status and no error (pty.rs:460-522). The host test checks that a Wayland disconnect preserves cleanup (main.rs:975-1021).
contract_checks.arguments: PASS. Exact flag order, absolute paths, socket 103 bytes or less (sun_path is checked again in connect), records path 1024 or less, lowercase hex48, seconds 1-120. Connect is bounded by min(deadline, 3 s) and is interruptible by a stop signal.

non_blocking_notes.N1_early_setup_has_no_cleanup_frame: Failures before the guarded closure write no CLEANUP frame: fd3 adopt, private_dir, or an application.json collision (main.rs:831-840). No child exists then. The session sees a missing CLEANUP, meaning incomplete, which fails closed but cannot tell 'no child created' from 'cleanup unknown'. This is allowed by the contract.
non_blocking_notes.N2_status_failure_not_in_result_json: result.json is written before CLEANUP is attempted, so a later status-channel failure appears only in status-error.json, stderr and exit 1, not in result.json errors. Consumers must read all three.
non_blocking_notes.N3_comment_scope: child-ready.json and grid-final.txt are written inside session(), before PTY cleanup. Their errors do not skip cleanup, but the comment at main.rs:870 ('Always cleanup before any fallible transcript/final-record operation') is broader than the code. These local file writes have no timeout.
non_blocking_notes.N4_shutdown_budget: After N seconds the shutdown tail is up to 250 ms TERM grace, 2 s reap, 250 ms final flush, plus fsyncs. Other inner bounds: readiness 20 s, exec 5 s, connect 3 s. The session's reserved shutdown budget must cover at least about 2.5 s plus I/O.
non_blocking_notes.N5_group_signal_after_shell_eof: The group target depends on getsid and getpgid succeeding at signal time. After a checked exec (the child proved sid==pgrp==pid), the unreaped leader keeps that group ID reserved. If this XNU's getsid or getpgid fail on an exited but unreaped leader (not verified here), only the leader is signalled, and leftover group members such as '&' commands are not. No background jobs are claimed; a Darwin orphan check would settle it.
non_blocking_notes.N6_pre_output_spin: While accepted input is pending but pty.ready() is false (exec checked, no PTY output yet), the master is polled for POLLOUT and the loop does not block. It is bounded by the first output or the deadlines. CPU only; latency is off-priority.
non_blocking_notes.N7_lenient_parsing_and_unfocused_keys: Rust u64 parsing accepts '+' and leading zeros in --seconds. A wl_keyboard.key without focus is ignored, producing no bytes, rather than treated as a protocol failure (input.rs:49-51). Neither can create input.
non_blocking_notes.N8_path_based_records: Files are opened by dir.join(name) after a path check, with no dirfd or openat, so O_NOFOLLOW protects only the final name. A same-UID swap of the directory between check and open is not excluded; the session-owned 0700 directory limits this. shm-N files are created in the same directory (O_EXCL, then unlinked), so a pre-existing shm-N name fails at first frame as a fault, not at launch. The directory itself is never fsynced (fine for same-boot reading).

evidence_gaps_for_admission: run() refuses non-Darwin targets (main.rs:823-828), so the full run() order (cleanup, transcript sync, result.json, CLEANUP) is established here by source reading only. Host tests cover session() and status framing separately.
DS4 host evidence is Linux /proc only. Darwin evidence that /bin/sh cannot reach fd3, the Wayland socket, logs or the keymap is still required.
Real chonkstep compositor, launch-chord ownership, two-client and shared-Shell integration are untested; the host tests use an in-test wayland-server with synthetic input.
The SDK and linker binding of root's arm64 build belongs to artifact admission (see the build.log warnings).
